audit.whatIsWrong: Six fields describe Sion's E as a shield-strip and refer to Teemo having a "W shield" — e.g. wants.foe[0] "follow with E to strip your W shield", whys[1] "His W shield into E strip combo", wants.you[2] "before his W shield regenerates", spikes[0].text "follow with E shield-break".
audit.why: Sion's E is Roar of the Slayer: it damages, slows and reduces ARMOUR of the first enemy hit, and knocks minions back — there is no shield interaction in it at all. Separately, Teemo's W is Move Quick, a movement-speed ability; Teemo has no shield for anything to strip. The only shield in the matchup is Sion's own Soul Furnace (W).
audit.corrected: Roar of the Slayer = armour shred + slow at 800 range. Sion's Soul Furnace (W) is the shield, and it reactivates after 3s for magic damage scaling on the target's max health.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sion.json (E Roar of the Slayer, W Soul Furnace)

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere states the range relationship, and full:phases[1].why claims "Q-blind erases his auto-trade window entirely".
audit.why: Roar of the Slayer has 800 range; Teemo's autos and Blinding Dart both reach 680. Sion can shred armour and slow from outside Teemo's entire threat range, which is the actual reason the early levels favour him. And living Sion's damage is Decimating Smash and Soul Furnace — both abilities — so a blind takes almost nothing off him in lane.
audit.corrected: Sion pokes from 800 to your 680. Blinding Dart is close to dead weight against living Sion; hold it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single highest-value use of Blinding Dart in this matchup is never named as such.
audit.why: Glory in Death (Sion's passive zombie form) is entirely rapid basic attacks that heal him and deal bonus damage based on the target's max health. Blinding Dart shuts basic attacks off, so it neutralises the whole reanimation — heal and damage together. This is where the blind should be banked, not spent in lane.
audit.corrected: Hold Blinding Dart for Glory in Death — zombie Sion is pure autos, so the blind removes both the heal and the max-HP burst.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sion.json (P Glory in Death: heal, percentHealth)

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flags "NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere"; sequencingCues = 0. breakdown.cooldowns said only "track it".
audit.why: Decimating Smash is 10/9/8/7/6s and Soul Furnace 15/14/13/12/11s. A whiffed charge at rank 1 is a 10-second window in which Sion has no way to touch a moving Teemo — that is the concrete trade cue the entry lacked.
audit.corrected: Poke the full 10s after a whiffed Decimating Smash; Soul Furnace is back in 15s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: "Liandry's Angueur" in content spikes[2].text and whys[5].
audit.why: No item of that name exists — it is a corruption of Liandry's. This entry's own full layer (report Itemization) already calls it Liandry's Torment, so the file contradicts itself.
Level 6 shroom spike, Nashor's first-item spike and the Heartsteel/Warmog's 2-item inversion are all present and match how the lane actually swings.

edits.before: Sion owns levels 1 through 3 because his charged Q is a direct counter to your camouflage passive — standing still to turn invisible is exactly what he wants you to do so he can walk up and knock you up from brush. Never proc your passive while he has Q available. His E also strips shields, but the real threat is that charged Q one-shot: stay at your max Toxic Shot auto range, move constantly, and never let him get a stationary read on you. Take poke trades with E autos and back off the moment his Q starts glowing — do not be in that radius when it releases.

edits.before: You win the extended game through split-push zone control, not direct combat. Sion's Heartsteel-Warmog's tank line means he eventually walks through a few mushrooms without dying, so your shroom walls must be deep in the jungle and at objective chokes — slow him down so your team can collapse, not so you can 1v1 him. Your Liandry's percent-health burn is still doing real work even into his stacked HP, and a Blinding Shot into his zombie passive auto burst is enough deterrence to keep him from hard-committing. Avoid any situation where his team can follow his R into you; the shroom map you have built should make that nearly impossible if you maintained vision discipline from level 6 onward.
